question: Should OpenClaw expose `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent` as a target-agent resource limit, and queue or reject excess native and ACP spawns through one shared enforcement path?
rationale: The use case and missing behavior are confirmed, but the public configuration shape, limit composition, and excess-work semantics establish a new scheduler contract that requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Add shared target cap
options.body: Introduce the nested per-agent setting and atomically enforce it across native and ACP spawns alongside existing global and per-parent limits.

options.title: Design unified lanes
options.body: Defer this capability into a broader named-lane policy that also resolves the related lane and inbound-agent concurrency requests.

options.title: Retain current controls
options.body: Keep only the global and requester-session caps and document that target-specific resource isolation is unsupported.

recommendation.title: Add shared target cap
recommendation.body: Introduce the nested per-agent setting and atomically enforce it across native and ACP spawns alongside existing global and per-parent limits.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail ties this person to the central concurrency defaults, resolver, and command-lane setup affected by the decision.
